comments.body:
PRE-EMPTIVE REMEDIATION before this ticket's first plan review, reading its criteria the way the
reviewer will. Four issues, none of which a keyword scan would have surfaced.

1. FILE_IMPACT WAS EMPTY. An unscoped attestation dies stale-head on EVERY commit — the failure mode
   that has already bitten epic 9227 on this branch. Set now, BEFORE the review, because setting it
   afterwards is a material edit that destroys a fresh PASS. Six paths, including
   src/rebar/_deprecations.py (see 3).

2. AC2's "fires exactly once per process" WAS ORDER-DEPENDENT. Once-per-process is module-level
   state: whichever test triggers the warning first consumes it, so a second in-process assertion
   observes zero warnings and PASSES FOR THE WRONG REASON. This is the same order-dependent
   blindness that forced d8ef's registry guard into a subprocess — the defect class recurring in a
   different subsystem. The AC now requires explicit isolation (subprocess, precedent
   tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py:115, or an explicit once-flag reset) and requires the plan
   to say which.

3. THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS — do not hand-roll a warning. src/rebar/_deprecations.py is a real
   registry (REGISTRY, Deprecation, _scheduled/_permanent, plus a tombstone path for removed inputs),
   and scripts/gen_env_registry.py already IMPORTS rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY and unions it into
   the generated env docs. So registering the deprecation there is what makes it appear in
   docs/env-vars.md automatically; a bespoke warnings.warn would be invisible to that generator.
   Added to file_impact so the implementer finds it.

4. AC5 WAS VACUOUS, and I verified that rather than assuming it. It required "the cutover runbook's
   kill-switch entry is expressed in class terms, with no reference to REBAR_LLM_MODEL as the
   recovery lever". MEASURED: `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL infra/runbooks/` returns NOTHING across all
   ten runbooks, so no runbook ever offered it as a recovery lever and the criterion would have
   passed with zero work. Retargeted to where the references actually are — the five docs that
   present REBAR_LLM_MODEL as the way to choose a model: llm-framework.md, config.md,
   plan-review-gate.md, workflow-authoring-v2.md, and the generated env-vars.md. The kill-switch
   entry stays with S8 (eb6e), which owns infra/runbooks/.

A CLAIM I MADE AND WITHDREW, recorded because the correction matters more than the claim. I first
read AC5 as a CIRCULAR DEPENDENCY: d23e needing a runbook entry that eb6e creates, while eb6e is
blocked behind eb58 which cannot close until d23e does. Checking instead of asserting showed
infra/runbooks/ ALREADY EXISTS with ten files including a kill-switch entry
(two-vote-gate-rollback.md), so eb6e adds an entry rather than creating the directory and there is
no deadlock. The real defect was vacuity, not circularity.

comments.body:
ROUND 1: BLOCK, four findings. ALL ACCEPTED, and two of them are my errors rather than gaps in the plan's ambition.

FINDINGS 1, 3 and 4 ARE ONE THEME: src/rebar/_deprecations.py was missing from the SCOPE section. I had put it in file_impact and then failed to name it in Scope — an internal inconsistency in my own ticket. And the omission mattered, because the codebase ENFORCES the mechanism rather than merely offering it:
  * registration goes through _scheduled(...) into REGISTRY (_deprecations.py:62, :100);
  * emission goes through warn_deprecated (:299);
  * tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py:125::test_no_raw_deprecation_emissions SOURCE-SCANS all of src/rebar/ and fails any deprecation signal that does not route through warn_deprecated.
So the plan as written — 'emit a deprecation warning in config.py' — would have failed an existing test, AND been invisible to scripts/gen_env_registry.py, which imports rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY and unions it into the generated env docs. Scope now states all of that with citations.

FINDING 2 IS THE ONE WORTH DWELLING ON: my 'MEASURED five files' enumeration was INCOMPLETE, and I had labelled it MEASURED. The review pointed at README.md:239. Re-measured across the WHOLE repo: there are SIX prose files, not five —
  README.md, docs/llm-framework.md, docs/config.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md,
  docs/workflow-authoring-v2.md, docs/env-vars.md (generated).
The one I missed is the PROJECT FRONT PAGE, and it is the most consequential of the six: README.md:239 presents REBAR_LLM_MODEL as THE documented multi-provider interface ('plus Gemini and OpenAI-compatible local servers like LMStudio/Ollama via REBAR_LLM_MODEL/...'). A deprecation ticket that missed it would have left the front door advertising the deprecated lever.

WHY I MISSED IT, because the mechanism is reusable and so is the mistake: I ran the grep scoped to `docs/ infra/` and wrote MEASURED against the result. The measurement was real; its SCOPE was wrong. Labelling something MEASURED does not make it COMPLETE — the scope of the measurement is part of the claim, and a repo-root file falls outside every subdirectory grep. This is the third time this session that a confidently-stated fact was wrong in a way only re-running it exposed (the others: plan_review_recovery.py:8's docstring, which is accurate, and a d23e 'circular dependency' that evaporated).

Both fixes applied; re-review running.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROUND 3: BLOCK, one finding, ACCEPTED — and checking the convention showed BOTH SIDES OF MY CONTRADICTION WERE WRONG.

THE FINDING: Approach said 'a migration window of one minor release' while Scope said the deprecation is registered with remove_in=_MAJOR (v1.0.0). Two different windows in one plan. I introduced the second half myself in round 1 while fixing a different finding — remediating one criterion and creating an inconsistency with another.

WHAT THE CONVENTION ACTUALLY IS, checked rather than chosen: ALL SIX existing env-var deprecations in _deprecations.REGISTRY use _permanent(...), NOT _scheduled(...) — REBAR_NO_SYNC, COMPACT_THRESHOLD, SCRATCH_BASE_DIR, REBAR_ACLI_TIMEOUT, RECONCILER_ABSENT_GET_BUDGET, REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE. _permanent sets remove_in=None with permanent=True: it warns and NEVER removes. So this repo's practice for a deprecated env var is to keep the old name working indefinitely and point at the replacement.

Neither 'one minor release' nor 'remove at v1.0.0' matched that. Had I simply picked a side of my own contradiction I would have shipped a plan that deviates from six precedents — and removing a documented env var is a breaking change, made worse here because this one is named on the project README. Adopted _permanent.

A SECOND PROBLEM DISSOLVED AS A RESULT, which is why the convention check was worth more than the fix: the S8 kill-switch DURABILITY concern from round 2 is now moot. I had argued that S8's runbook naming REBAR_LLM_MODEL would rot when the variable was removed at the next major. Under a permanent alias it is never removed, so the runbook never rots, and expressing the kill switch in class terms drops from 'needed for durability' to 'preferable for coherence'. The eb6e note has been corrected accordingly — I would rather withdraw a concern than leave a stale argument standing on another ticket.

Round-by-round on this ticket: (1) _deprecations.py missing from Scope + a MEASURED enumeration that missed README.md; (2) fan-out placed in the wrong module + the S8 cross-ticket conflict; (3) a window contradiction I introduced in round 1. Every finding legitimate, and rounds 1 and 3 were both self-inflicted while fixing something else — the cost of editing a plan under review pressure rather than re-reading the whole thing after each change.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRE-EMPTIVE, to be applied AFTER round 7 returns (comment, not an edit — round 7 is in flight and a material edit would void its verdict).

EXACT READ-SITE ENUMERATION, run rather than assumed. In `llm/config.py` the ONLY env read of REBAR_LLM_MODEL is `:469`. `:10` and `:195` are docstrings (already Scope'd), and `:470` is a DIFFERENT variable, REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER — easy to miscount as a second read. VERIFIED that `:469` really is an env read: `_llm_str` calls `os.environ.get(env_name)` in its body. Also verified there is NO alias-resolver path — neither `src/rebar/config.py` nor `_config_schema.py` mentions the var, so `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` is not involved. So the two-site rule (config.py:469 + the new model_classes read) is COMPLETE, not merely better than one site.

A DESIGN NUANCE THE PLAN SHOULD PIN, because a reviewer will ask and the answer is not obvious: `_llm_str`'s precedence is CLI > env > file > default, and it RETURNS EARLY on a CLI hit — so when `--model` wins, `os.environ.get` is never called at all. Two possible semantics follow:
  (a) warn whenever REBAR_LLM_MODEL is SET, even if CLI overrode it; or
  (b) warn only when the env value actually WINS precedence.
(b) cannot be implemented inside `_llm_str` — that helper is shared by roughly a dozen variables and must not learn about one of them. Implementing (b) would mean duplicating the precedence check at the call site, which is the same duplication the plan already rejects for the fan-out.
CHOOSE (a): check `os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_MODEL") is not None` at the `:469` call site and warn. An operator who has exported a deprecated variable should be told so even when a CLI flag happens to override it this run — the export is still a migration item. State this explicitly in the plan, and add the matching test: `--model` set AND REBAR_LLM_MODEL set -> CLI value wins AND the warning still fires. Without that test, (a) and (b) are indistinguishable to the suite and an implementer could silently ship either.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRE-EMPTIVE DESIGN REFINEMENT, to apply after round 9 returns (comment, not an edit — round 9 is in flight). Found by reading the actual insertion point rather than assuming it.

WHERE THE FAN-OUT GOES, confirmed implementable in ONE line. `_parse_slot` (`model_classes.py:145`) applies the documented per-field precedence:
    model = raw.get("model") or _DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS[name]
    model = _cli_override(...) or _env_override(...) or model
i.e. CLI > per-class env > config table > built-in default. A bare REBAR_LLM_MODEL belongs at the DEFAULT position — replacing `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS[name]` with the env value when set. That yields CLI > per-class env (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL etc.) > config table > REBAR_LLM_MODEL > built-in default, which satisfies BOTH existing ACs: explicit class config still wins, and the bare var alone still maps to all three classes. No new precedence logic, no duplication.

BUT THE PLAN LEAVES A REAL AMBIGUITY THAT WOULD PRODUCE NOISY OUTPUT. `_parse_slot` is invoked ONCE PER CLASS by `parse_class_slots`, so a read-and-warn placed inside it fires THREE TIMES per `load_class_slots()` call — three identical deprecation warnings for one slot build. Under the accepted per-call semantics that is not incorrect, but it is bad output and the plan does not say which way to go, so an implementer could reasonably ship it.

REFINEMENT: read `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` ONCE in `parse_class_slots` (the single caller that loops the three classes), emit the ONE `warn_deprecated` call there, and pass the resolved fallback default DOWN into `_parse_slot` as a parameter. Properties: one warning per slot build rather than three; still per-call with NO dedup state, so the withdrawn once-per-process machinery stays withdrawn; the literal `os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_MODEL")` stays in `model_classes.py` so it remains visible to `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, whose AST scan only records STRING-LITERAL env names (verified in that generator's source); and `_parse_slot` keeps its per-field precedence untouched.

ADD THE MATCHING TEST, because 'three warnings' vs 'one warning' is exactly the kind of thing no existing criterion would catch: with REBAR_LLM_MODEL set and no classes configured, ONE `load_class_slots()` call emits EXACTLY ONE warning, not one per class. Note this is a per-CALL count assertion, NOT once-per-process — a second `load_class_slots()` call must warn again.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROUND 9 = PASS (0 blocking, 9 advisory). Attestation SIGNED and CERTIFIED at 2b5bb00cdf5f559ea644e3c853cd97cbc2220bc8; ticket CLAIMED. Nine rounds total.

DECISION ON THE QUEUED REFINEMENT — carried into IMPLEMENTATION rather than into the plan, deliberately. The refinement (read REBAR_LLM_MODEL ONCE in `parse_class_slots` and pass the default down, instead of once per class inside `_parse_slot`, so one `load_class_slots()` call emits ONE warning rather than three) is an implementation choice that the certified plan PERMITS rather than contradicts: Scope requires the fan-out and its literal env read to live in `model_classes.py`, and `parse_class_slots` is in `model_classes.py`. Editing the plan to mandate it would be a MATERIAL edit, invalidating a PASS that took nine rounds, to specify something no AC constrains and that I am about to implement correctly anyway.

So it is recorded HERE as the binding implementation decision, and it will be enforced by a TEST rather than by plan text: one `load_class_slots()` call with the variable set emits EXACTLY ONE warning. That is a per-CALL count, NOT once-per-process — a second call must warn again, since the once-per-process requirement was withdrawn as unmechanised. If a future reader wonders why the plan is silent on warning multiplicity, this is why.

compiled_state.description:
# Deprecate REBAR_LLM_MODEL, add ADR and example configs

## Context / Problem
Once classes are the interface, `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is a second, ambiguous way to say the same thing —
a single scalar that cannot express a per-tier mapping. Keeping both indefinitely reintroduces the
ambiguity this epic removes. It is also load-bearing today: the production cutover's kill switch
[rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] is documented as "point `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back at `anthropic:...`".

## Approach
Deprecate with a MIGRATION WINDOW, registered via `_scheduled(...)` with the default `remove_in=_MAJOR` (v1.0.0). THIS IS THE PARENT'S DECISION, not a default I chose: eb58 states in bold that "`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is DEPRECATED with a migration window rather than kept as a permanent alias", with the rationale that there are few clients today and it is a single-scalar knob. An earlier draft switched to `_permanent(...)` because all six existing env deprecations use it — a real observation, but the WRONG authority AND a miscategorisation. The registry itself says those six are kept forever because they are RENAMES of established names (`_deprecations.py:71-73`); `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is a SUPERSESSION by a different interface, which is what `_scheduled` is for. The parent CONSIDERED the permanent alias and rejected it deliberately, so the six precedents are the repo's general habit and this is a considered exception. Approach and Scope now agree on the window. Within the window `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is still
honoured, emits a deprecation warning through `warn_deprecated` (per call — see AC2, the once-per-process form was withdrawn as unmechanised), and maps to ALL THREE classes — the
widest-compatibility reading, so an operator who set one model keeps getting exactly that model
everywhere and nothing breaks mid-window.

Deprecation (rather than keeping it as a permanent shorthand) is a deliberate operator-approved call:
there are few clients today, and it yields a single unambiguous config model.

Because the kill switch's current wording goes stale the moment this lands, rewriting it in class
terms is part of THIS ticket's contract — a kill switch that is wrong during an incident is worse than
none.

Ships example configs per provider in docs, so the easy path is documentation rather than presets
shipped in code that clients select by name.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — **HOSTS A `warn_deprecated` CALL AT ITS OWN ENV READ (`:469`), plus the
  docstring corrections at `:10` and `:195`.** Two earlier drafts both got this wrong and the reasoning
  matters, so it is recorded: draft 1 put the call here and ONLY here, which misses the fan-out path;
  draft 2 over-corrected to model_classes.py ONLY, claiming "one call site at the read covers every
  reachable path". THAT CLAIM IS FALSE. VERIFIED: `config.py:469` performs its own read —
  `_llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_MODEL", "model", DEFAULT_MODEL)` inside `from_env()` — so a
  model_classes-only warning is silent on every path that builds a config without touching the
  fan-out.
  AND THE WARNING CANNOT LIVE IN `resolve_model_string` AT ALL, which is the deeper reason: `:205-207`
  calls `resolve_model_string(step or workflow or cfg.model)`, passing an ALREADY-RESOLVED STRING. By
  that point the value is indistinguishable from a config-table `model` key or a per-step `model:` —
  so warning there would fire FALSELY for operators who never set the env var at all. Provenance
  exists ONLY at the env read. Therefore: **the warning goes at EVERY env read of `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`
  and nowhere else** — `config.py:469` today, plus the new read in `model_classes.py` that the fan-out
  needs. Two call sites is CORRECT and costs nothing, because emission is per-call by design (AC2) and
  needs no dedup.
  `config.py` must still NOT host the class fan-out:
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — **the map-to-all-three fan-out belongs HERE, and it READS
  `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` ITSELF** (a literal `os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_MODEL")`, exactly as `:118-126`
  already reads the nine per-class vars — which is also what keeps it visible to
  `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, whose AST scan only records STRING-LITERAL env names). Reading it
  here is what gives this site the provenance needed to warn correctly, and it carries the second
  `warn_deprecated` call, beside the slot
  resolution it has to compose with: `load_class_slots` (`:207`), `parse_class_slots` (`:166`) and
  `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS` (`:47`). A bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` becomes the default for all three slots
  at the point slots are built, which is also where the documented per-field precedence
  (CLI > env > config table > built-in default) is already applied — putting it in `config.py`
  behind a lazy import would duplicate that precedence logic on the far side of the seam.
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — **REQUIRED, and previously missing from this Scope.** The
  deprecation must be REGISTERED here via `_scheduled(...)` in `REGISTRY` (`:62`, `:100`) and emitted
  through `warn_deprecated` (`:299`), per the parent's migration-window decision. **AND THE BLOCK COMMENT AT `:75-79` MUST BE CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE** — previously
  unscoped, and adding the entry makes it FALSE. It currently reads: "This registry now holds ONLY
  these permanent renames: every remaining SCHEDULED (removable) surface has been removed in the
  pre-1.0 breaking passes." This ticket adds the FIRST scheduled entry since that drain, so the
  comment must say so instead of asserting the registry is permanent-only.
  **WHY `_scheduled` IS RIGHT HERE AND THE SIX `_permanent` PRECEDENTS DO NOT APPLY — this closes the
  question, which has been flipped twice.** The registry documents its own reason for those six at
  `:71-73`: they are "stable REBAR_-prefixed renames of established names" that "warned 'deprecated'
  historically, which was a contradiction — they are kept forever." That is a RENAME: the same knob
  under a better name, so it must never be removed. `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is NOT a rename — it is a knob
  SUPERSEDED by a different interface (per-class slots), which is precisely what `_scheduled` exists
  for and what the two pre-1.0 breaking passes recorded at `:87-99` actually used and then drained.
  So the six precedents are precedent for RENAMES, not for supersessions, and an earlier draft of this
  plan that switched to `_permanent` on the strength of their COUNT was wrong twice over: it
  contradicted the parent's explicit decision AND miscategorised the change. State this reasoning in
  the corrected comment so the next reader does not re-litigate it. This is ENFORCED, not stylistic:
  `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py:125::test_no_raw_deprecation_emissions` source-scans all
  of `src/rebar/` and fails any deprecation signal that does not route through `warn_deprecated`.
  A hand-rolled `warnings.warn` in `config.py` would fail that test AND be invisible to
  `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, which imports `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` and unions it into the
  generated env docs.
- **USER-FACING STRINGS presenting `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the CURRENT interface — previously missing from
  this Scope, and NOT mere comments.** I earlier cleared these as "comments/docstrings, inert"; that
  was WRONG for the first two, which render to operators:
  * `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:160` — the `argparse` `description=` for `rebar review`, i.e.
    `--help` TEXT: "Needs the 'agents' extra + a model API key (provider per REBAR_LLM_MODEL)".
  * `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:64` — an MCP TOOL DESCRIPTION surfaced to MCP clients.
  * `src/rebar/llm/config.py:10` — the module docstring's env table, presenting it as "model id
    (default ``claude-opus-4-8``)", i.e. THE model knob.
  * `src/rebar/llm/config.py:195` — `resolve_model`'s docstring, describing it as current precedence.
  `llm/completion.py:72` and `llm/gate_context.py:14` are genuinely internal comments and need no edit.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the class model and the deprecation window.
- `docs/` — example configs (Anthropic-only, Bedrock-only, mixed-provider, local+fallback).
- ~~The cutover runbook's kill-switch entry — restated in class terms.~~ **REMOVED FROM SCOPE, and
  this resolves a contradiction in an earlier draft.** The S8 section below states that this ticket
  does NOT redesign S8's recovery path, and `infra/runbooks/` is deliberately absent from
  `file_impact` — yet Scope listed the runbook restatement as a deliverable here. It belongs to S8
  (`eb6e`), which owns `infra/runbooks/`. This ticket's only obligation toward it is the durability
  note already recorded on `eb6e` for the operator to resolve there.

## Testing
Unit tier for the mapping and the warning; docs assertions for the rest.
- `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set and no classes configured: all three classes resolve to that model.
- BOTH env-read paths warn, tested SEPARATELY — this is the round-6 defect and needs a test each:
  (a) `config.from_env()` with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set and the fan-out never invoked -> warns (the
      `config.py:469` read);
  (b) `load_class_slots()` / `resolve_model_string()` reached WITHOUT `config.from_env()` -> warns (the
      `model_classes.py` read). A model_classes-only or config-only implementation passes one and fails
      the other, which is exactly the gap two earlier drafts shipped.
- CLI PRECEDENCE, pinned because two semantics are possible and the suite cannot tell them apart
  otherwise: `_llm_str` resolves CLI > env > file > default and RETURNS EARLY on a CLI hit, so
  `os.environ.get` is never reached when `--model` wins. THE CHOSEN SEMANTIC IS WARN-WHEN-SET —
  check `os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_MODEL") is not None` at the `:469` call site. An operator who has
  exported a deprecated variable should be told even when a CLI flag overrides it this run, because the
  export is still a migration item. Warn-when-env-WINS is rejected: it cannot live inside `_llm_str`,
  which serves ~a dozen variables and must not learn about one of them, and implementing it at the call
  site would duplicate the precedence logic this plan already refuses to duplicate for the fan-out.
  TEST: `--model` set AND `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set -> the CLI value wins AND the warning still fires.
- NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the reason the warning cannot live in `resolve_model_string`: a config-table
  `model` key (or a per-step `model:`) with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` UNSET must emit NO warning. A warning
  placed on the resolved string would fire here falsely.
- the deprecation warning is emitted whenever `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is consulted, PER CALL. Not
  once-per-process: that requirement was withdrawn (see AC2) because `warn_deprecated` has no dedup
  and none of the six existing env deprecations has any either.
- classes configured AND `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set: classes win, warning still emitted.
- with neither set, resolution is unchanged from today's defaults.

## Interaction with S8's kill switch (eb6e) — NOT a safety conflict, but it must be handled

S8 (`eb6e`) documents its production recovery path as "a documented one-line kill switch
(`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back to `anthropic:…`)", scopes `infra/compose/` and `infra/runbooks/` around it,
and has an AC to EXECUTE it end-to-end. S8 is blocked behind `eb58`, which cannot close until THIS
ticket does — so the deprecation lands FIRST and S8 would then build a recovery path on a deprecated
variable.

**That does not break the kill switch, and this ticket must not be read as breaking it.** VERIFIED: `_scheduled(...)` sets `permanent=False` with `remove_in=_MAJOR` (v1.0.0), so within the window the variable WARNS and keeps working — S8's kill switch is unaffected BY THIS TICKET. But be exact about the limit, because an earlier draft of this plan overclaimed here: under a migration window `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` IS scheduled for removal, so any S8 runbook naming it as the recovery lever WILL rot at v1.0.0. That durability concern is REAL, is recorded on eb6e for the operator to resolve there, and was briefly withdrawn by a draft that had switched to `_permanent` — reverting to the parent's window reinstates it. This ticket does NOT redesign S8's recovery path.

The paragraph above is the CURRENT and FINAL position on durability. An earlier UPDATE block here claimed the concern "dissolves under the permanent-alias decision" — written while this plan briefly used `_permanent`, and now WRONG, because the parent's window means the variable IS scheduled for removal. So the resolution is documentation, not mechanism — no change to S8's safety behaviour:

- this ticket's docs criterion covers recovery documentation too, so nothing it writes presents the
  deprecated variable as the way to recover;
- `eb6e` should express its kill switch in CLASS terms (the class slots, or
  `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL`), which is a strictly equivalent one-line operator action. Recorded as a
  comment on `eb6e` rather than edited into it, since redesigning another ticket's production
  recovery path is the operator's call and not a side effect of a deprecation ticket.
